newsitem.title: USA: A.G. Edwards says it is not a target of muni probe.
newsitem.headline: A.G. Edwards says it is not a target of muni probe.

text.p: A.G. Edwards & Co on Thursday said that it did not believe it was a target of probe into an alleged scheme by a former treasurer of Essex County, New Jersey, to get kickbacks for steering business to two firms.

Earlier the U.S. Attorney's Office in Newark said it filed charges against the former official, Joseph Galluzzi of Springfield, N.J., alleging he took kickbacks from A.G. Edwards and First Fidelity Securities, now a unit of First Union Corp.

"Based on conversations with the office of the U.S. attorney, we do not believe that our firm is the target of any current investigation in connection with the referenced payment or other matters related to Mr. Galluzi," A.G. Edwards said in a statement.

The company said it "cooperated fully" with the U.S. Attorney and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, which filed a companion case against Galluzzi alleging violations of U.S. securities laws.

Further, the company said it believed an individual "referenced" in the indictment was a municipal investment banker in the A.G. Edward's Newark public finance office. The banker is on administrative leave, it said.
"The individual was not named in the indictment and we do not think it is appropriate to disclose the individual's name," the company said.
The criminal charges allege Galluzzi received $170,000 in kickbacks from First Fidelity Securities and $15,000 from A.G. Edwards & Co in Newark, a unit of A.G. Edwards Inc.
First Fidelity, without admitting or denying guilt, settled allegations related to the matter by paying penalties and fees of almost $2.3 million.
